action_categories.definition: Reads and emits file or code contents, including textual content or rendered binary bytes, either wholly or by selected lines, ranges, heads, tails, or byte regions. In compound events, apply this category to each distinct content-display operation. A downstream display stage that emits selected source or file lines from search output also qualifies when those lines are visibly displayed.
exclude: Searching text or paths without a separate content-display operation
A search command whose output is not separately displayed as file or code content
Inspecting metadata such as size, permissions, or file type
Merely creating or running a file without displaying its contents
include: cat, head, tail, sed, od, xxd, or equivalent used to display file contents, code, or byte regions
Displaying source, header, script, configuration, generated-table, or binary-input contents
Applying alongside ACT_SEARCH_TEXT when a command searches and a separate stage displays selected file or code lines

action_categories.definition: Enumerates directory or collection entries without applying a substantive content predicate. Long-format enumeration may also receive ACT_INSPECT_METADATA when metadata fields are substantively observed. Do not infer ACT_CHECK_PATH_EXISTS merely because a listing succeeds.
exclude: Checking whether one specifically named path exists as the primary purpose
A metadata query on one specified artifact without enumeration
include: ls or equivalent directory listing
Listing source, output, configuration, build, or script directories
Listing entries matched by a directory or file glob
Listing specifically named files or scripts as entries without reading their contents

action_categories.definition: Traverses paths to find files or directories selected by name, type, extension, or other path predicates.
exclude: Locating one executable by command lookup
Checking whether a specified path exists
include: find or equivalent recursive or path-pattern search
Locating files with a given extension or matching a filename pattern
Searching for heterogeneous file types, with each matched object category assigned when supported

action_categories.definition: Searches file contents or emitted text for literal text, symbols, identifiers, constants, or regular-expression matches. Apply alongside ACT_READ_CONTENT when the same compound event also displays selected content or search-result lines through a separate display stage.
exclude: Displaying a selected code or byte region without a search predicate
include: grep, rg, or equivalent content search
Searching for function names, macros, compiler flags, parser symbols, options, include directives, diagnostics, or other text
Filtering command output by a textual predicate
A pipeline that searches source or emitted text and separately limits or displays matching lines

action_categories.definition: Checks whether a specified file, directory, or artifact is present or absent. A listing or glob is not itself an existence check unless presence or absence of the named path is an explicit observable purpose.
exclude: Enumerating directory contents without an explicit presence check
Checking whether a tool is installed by command lookup
include: Existence tests or commands whose observable purpose is presence checking
Checking for a build directory, script, or executable artifact
Checking several named paths for presence

action_categories.definition: Inspects filesystem or binary metadata such as permissions, size, executable status, timestamps, or file type. Apply alongside ACT_LIST_ENTRIES when long-format listing substantively exposes metadata, including in compound commands.
exclude: Counting lines as the sole operation
include: ls -l, stat, file, or equivalent metadata inspection
Examining an executable's mode, size, timestamps, or inferred type
Inspecting metadata for a source file, generated table, binary input, or build artifact
Applying the category whenever reported metadata is an observable result, even if enumeration is also performed

action_categories.definition: Checks whether required commands or dependencies are available for use. Apply when availability is an explicit observable purpose; it may co-occur with ACT_INSPECT_TOOLCHAIN when the same event also reports a resolved path, identity, or version.
exclude: Detailed inspection of tool versions, identities, or resolved paths when availability is not also an explicit purpose
A command lookup whose emitted path or identity is reported without an explicit availability check
include: Boolean availability or package-presence checks
Checking for a build system, compiler, interpreter, utility, or package
A command lookup explicitly used both to establish availability and to report the resolved command

action_categories.definition: Reports installed tool, compiler, or command identity, location, or version details.
exclude: A boolean availability check with no identity, location, or version inspection
include: Compiler or utility version queries and command-location reporting
Output that identifies a command or reports its resolved path or version, even when the same lookup also establishes availability
Inspecting compiler, interpreter, or build-helper locations

action_categories.definition: Counts lines in one or more files, including generated tables, source files, and headers. Apply whenever line count is an observable result, even with other metadata operations. When files have different types, assign all applicable object categories.
exclude: General metadata inspection when no line count is produced
include: wc -l or equivalent line-count operation
Measuring implementation, header, generated, or amalgamated files
Counting lines in a generated table, source file, or header

action_categories.definition: Creates or configures build-system state, options, directories, prefixes, or targets without performing the build itself.
include: Meson, CMake, or equivalent configuration or setup invocation
Configuring a build directory, enabling binaries, or selecting a prefix

action_categories.definition: Invokes compilation, linking, installation, packaging, or a build script whose operative purpose is to produce software artifacts.
exclude: Creating a directory or writing an input file as supporting operations
include: Compiler, make, ninja, or project compile-script execution
Compiling targets, linking fuzzers, installing built project outputs, or packaging generated artifacts

action_categories.definition: Installs or updates external packages, libraries, or development tools.
include: Package-manager installation or dependency setup
Installing a build system, compiler dependency, runtime, or development header package

action_categories.definition: Creates a directory path, including parent directories when requested. In compound events, apply this category independently of tool availability or toolchain inspection performed by the same event.
exclude: Writing a file into an already existing directory
A directory created only implicitly by another operation
include: mkdir or equivalent directory-creation operation
Creating an output, build, temporary, or data directory

action_categories.definition: Creates or writes file contents, including binary data redirected to a new test or output file. This category concerns a newly created destination or a file-population operation and may co-occur with execution when the file is immediately used as input.
exclude: Editing an already existing file as the primary operation
Only printing data without file output
Running a program using an already existing input without writing it
include: Redirection, byte emission, or file-writing operation that creates or populates a file
Writing a PoC binary, generated bytes, or a new script
Creating a binary fixture later supplied to a program
Creating a new destination by copying or saving file contents

action_categories.definition: Changes an existing file's contents, permissions, or placement as an intentional mutation. Apply to existing sources or destinations; a compound event may also receive ACT_WRITE_FILE when it creates a new destination.
exclude: Writing a new test input without modifying an existing file
include: Rewriting an existing script, applying an edit, changing mode, or overwriting an existing file
Adding cleanup commands to a build script or making it executable
Copying or moving a modified file when the operation intentionally changes an existing file or its placement

action_categories.definition: Constructs or derives in-memory test data and emits its representation without necessarily writing a file.
exclude: Writing the generated data to a file
Displaying bytes read from an existing file rather than constructing them
include: Constructing and printing bytes, headers, signatures, metadata fields, or structured test values
Constructing binary header components or image metadata and printing hexadecimal or structured representations

action_categories.definition: Runs a fuzzing or fuzz-harness executable, optionally with a supplied input or corpus. Apply to the execution even when the event also creates, reads, or searches the input or output.
include: Invoking a fuzzer binary or fuzz harness against input, redirected data, or a corpus
Running a decompression, parser, or structure-aware fuzzer
Running a fuzzer on a newly written PoC or seed file

action_categories.definition: Invokes a validation driver that coordinates checks such as preparation, patch application, restoration, or staged test execution.
include: Running a named validation script or validator with task-specific options
Invoking a validator with a PoC file or stage-selection flags

action_categories.definition: Emits an explicit diagnostic, root-cause statement, or analysis conclusion as output.
exclude: Reading code that contains a diagnosis
Running a test that merely produces diagnostic output without an explicit authored conclusion
include: Printing a labeled diagnosis or stated cause
Emitting a root-cause sentence about an unsafe copy or parser condition

action_categories.definition: Creates, displays, or changes a structured task, todo, checklist, or progress list.
include: Todo-list creation or status updates
Marking analysis complete or leaving patch and retest items pending

action_categories.definition: Reads version-control history or repository state to inspect commits, logs, revisions, or related historical records.
include: git log, git show, equivalent history queries, or commands that report repository revisions
Inspecting recent commits or historical changes

message_roles.definition: A message event whose observable text is empty and contains no substantive discourse content.
exclude: Nonempty explanations, diagnoses, plans, or reports
include: Message events with text equal to an empty string
An emitted message with empty text

message_roles.definition: An event explicitly typed or emitted as an error without requiring a command or textual payload.
exclude: Command output that merely contains an error string
A normal message describing a failure
include: Error events with null or absent command, output, and text fields
An error record containing only the error event type

message_subjects.definition: No observable message subject or topic is present.
exclude: Messages containing an identifiable topic, diagnosis, task, command, or result
include: Empty agent messages and error records without a textual subject
Empty text, null text, or labels such as none, no_content, or unspecified

object_categories.definition: A filesystem directory or directory collection used as a location, search root, listing target, or artifact collection. Assign this category to explicitly targeted directories; separately assign categories for named files or artifacts listed within them.
exclude: A single file or executable inside a directory
A directory inferred only from the presence of a file
include: Build, source, output, configuration, data, script, or backup directories
Directories used as listing targets or collections of files
A directory created, searched, listed, or used as a build or artifact location

object_categories.definition: A program implementation file containing source code, including amalgamated or generated source intended for compilation. For heterogeneous operations, assign this category whenever an implementation file is among the targets, even if headers or other object types are also targeted.
exclude: A selected symbol or code region when treated as the target
include: C, C++, or other implementation source files
Parser, decoder, or amalgamated implementation files
A source file counted, read, searched, or inspected for metadata
Implementation files returned by a heterogeneous path search

object_categories.definition: A header, interface, declaration, or type-definition file. For heterogeneous operations, assign this category whenever a header is among the targets, even if implementation source files or other object types are also targeted.
include: Public or internal headers and declaration files
.h files containing APIs, structs, masks, or constants
A header counted, read, searched, or inspected for metadata
Header files returned by a heterogeneous path search

object_categories.definition: An executable script that orchestrates preparation, building, running, or testing. A script remains this object category when it is merely listed, searched for, or read.
exclude: Static build configuration without executable orchestration
include: Shell, Python, or equivalent operational scripts
Build, preparation, execution, test, or validator scripts
Named scripts returned by a directory listing

object_categories.definition: Declarative build-system configuration or project build-definition content.
include: Meson, CMake, Make, or equivalent build files and option definitions
Project configuration, target declarations, and fuzzer build options

object_categories.definition: Configuration describing a patch task, immutable paths, target repository, or validation parameters.
include: Task or validator configuration files
TOML or JSON settings naming a target tree or protected test directory

object_categories.definition: A referenced function, loop, macro, constant, structure, line range, or other identifiable code element.
exclude: The containing file when the file itself is the target
A generated table treated as a file artifact
include: Search or inspection targets within source or headers
A decoder function, buffer-copy loop, macro, or line range

object_categories.definition: A generated lookup table, include artifact, or table-generator output used as code or data.
include: Generated type, bracket, mirroring, joining, or other lookup tables
Generated include or table files and their lookup macros
A generated table counted, read, searched, or inspected for metadata

object_categories.definition: An installed command, compiler, build helper, or utility invoked, located, or version-inspected.
exclude: A project-produced fuzzer or test binary when it is the execution target
include: Compilers, build tools, package tools, interpreters, and helper commands
Commands whose availability, resolved location, identity, or version is inspected
A command whose resolved path is reported by a lookup

object_categories.definition: A project-produced executable, library, archive, corpus, or collection of generated build outputs.
exclude: An input file supplied to a test
include: Fuzzer binaries, example binaries, archives, symbolizers, and output-directory artifact collections
A build output directory containing executables and seed archives
A compiled executable identified or inspected as a build output

object_categories.definition: Source code implementing a fuzz entry point and its input-to-library or parser mapping.
include: LLVM-style fuzz entrypoints and dedicated fuzz harness implementations
A function allocating from input bytes and calling a decoder

object_categories.definition: A binary file, byte sequence, PoC, seed, or test input supplied to a program. A newly created fixture remains this object category when it is then used as execution input.
exclude: In-memory bytes merely printed without being used as input
Generated data never materialized or supplied as input
include: Generated PoC files, redirected binary inputs, seed files, and byte sequences used as execution input
A short compressed-like input or parser test file
A binary fixture that is created, inspected, or passed to a fuzzer

object_categories.definition: An external package, library, runtime, or development dependency considered for installation or availability.
exclude: A project source file or built artifact
include: Package names and toolchain dependencies
A build-system package, compiler runtime, or development library

object_categories.definition: A structured checklist, todo list, or progress payload representing work items and statuses.
include: Created or updated task lists
Investigation, PoC, patch, and retest items

object_categories.definition: An explicit authored technical explanation of a suspected cause or defect.
exclude: Raw sanitizer output without an authored conclusion
include: Root-cause statements and concise defect explanations
A statement identifying an unsafe buffer-copy source

object_categories.definition: In-memory or transiently emitted generated data, such as byte sequences, encoded signatures, headers, or structured metadata, that is not treated as a file or execution input.
exclude: Generated data written to a file
A generated lookup table or other persistent build artifact
include: Generated bytes or structured fields printed directly
Constructed signatures, header data, serialized fragments, and other test representations

object_categories.definition: Version-control history or repository revision records used to inspect prior changes or commit state.
exclude: A working-tree directory without historical information
include: Commit logs, commit objects, revisions, and historical diffs
History returned by version-control history queries
